text:
jordan park: hey team, new hire here. got my Ventura MBP (M2) and did the Kandji/ABM flow. enrollment shows as 'Pending configuration' and mac says 'System extension blocked' for our VPN. when i try FileVault it errors: 'Escrow attempt failed: connection timeout'. okta shows device not compliant. any quick hints?
it-help: welcome jordan :wave: first off, which network were you on during setup (home vs RWD-Corp)? also can you paste output of:
```
profiles status -type configuration
sudo fdesetup status
scutil --get LocalHostName
```
avoid posting full serials here; we only need last 4 if we need to lookup in console.
jordan park: set up at home on my router. outputs:
profiles status -type configuration: Enrolled to kandji: true; profiles: com.redwood.mdm present; com.redwood.security missing
sudo fdesetup status: FileVault is Off
scutil --get LocalHostName: Jordans-MBP
security-bot: automated check: if system clock/timezone is off, SCEP can fail. run `sudo systemsetup -gettimezone` and `ntpdate -q time.apple.com` to verify.
kevin tran: +1 — home networks sometimes block SCEP or have MTU issues. jordan, go to System Settings -> Privacy & Security and tap 'Allow' for any system extension prompts, then reconnect to RWD-Corp (or tether to phone) and retry. if the certificate chain didn't install, Okta will mark device non-compliant. we can also push the com.redwood.security profile from Kandji if you provide last 4 of serial.
jordan park: ran timezone check, timezone is correct and ntp query succeeded. i rebooted and saw one 'System extension blocked' banner and allowed it. Kandji still says 'Pending configuration' and Okta still non-compliant. last 4 of serial: 7F2D
it-help: creating ticket NH-20260401-11 and assigning to endpoint. before pushing, try this flow: open Safari and visit https://kandji.redwood/setup-cert which will attempt an inline cert install (forces intermediate CA). then run `profiles renew -type enrollment`.
jordan park: visited the URL, got a certificate prompt, accepted. ran profiles renew -> now it shows com.redwood.security present. tried fdesetup again and got a new error: 'Escrow attempt failed: TLS handshake failed'.
kevin tran: TLS handshake error usually means SCEP traffic being intercepted or blocked (corporate PKI expects direct outbound to our SCEP gateway). since you're remote, home ISP might be doing DNS interception. try switching DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8, reconnect and try `profiles renew` again. also check Keychain Access -> Certificates to confirm 'Redwood Corporate CA' exists.
jordan park: switched DNS to 1.1.1.1, renewed profile, profile shows active. Keychain has "Redwood Corporate CA". ran `sudo fdesetup enable` -> it prompted for my username, then threw 'Escrow failed: server error (502)'.
it-help: 502 from escrow service means it hit our gateway but backend responded with error; i've escalated to infra team and opened remote session option. quick workaround: we can grant temporary admin so you can use the portal manual escrow flow (one-time recovery key) while infra investigates. want that?
jordan park: yes please, that would be great — got a few apps to install and blocked by admin prompts.
it-help: temporary admin granted for 2 hours. also added infra and security to ticket. you should see a Kandji prompt to install updates; approve needed system extensions.
jordan park: approved extensions, re-ran fdesetup and now it says FileVault is On. Okta turned compliant after a sync. thanks for the quick help y'all :thumbsup:
